clue.text: Stereotypical movies featuring characters as in fleeing Biloxi plantation

indicators.note: the letters (characters) of the place are to be taken and rearranged as needed
the word in runs away, so its letters leave the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A film genre about characters running away from a plantation in Biloxi, Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of BILOXI PLANTATION, let I and N (the word 'in') flee, and rearrange what is left. 'featuring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a 1970s American film genre built on racial stereotypes of Black characters.

clue.text: Express hatred with fun by firing European figures

indicators.note: to figure is to work out, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Showing loathing for people by having fun setting European statues alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning a dummy of a hated person is a traditional public show of hatred.

clue.text: Reason with a bad egg; there's nothing lost

indicators.note: the nothing is lost, so it is taken out

parts.note: a bad egg is a rogue
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.surface: Trying to reason with a villain when nothing is lost by it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to argue, making a case logically in a discussion.

clue.text: Susan's sloppy modern monologue rising to the peak of poetry

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: rap is a modern spoken rhymed performance

indicators.note: sloppily put together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Susan's careless rap rising to the summit of poetic achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Parnassus was sacred to Apollo and the Muses, so it stands for the height of poetry.

clue.text: Before the house agents, nothing dodgy

parts.note: O is the zero shape for nothing

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Estate agents doing a house viewing and nothing dodgy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' suggests property, but it means a theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers are in front of the theatre audience, the house, when on the boards.

clue.text: Having something of pitch, can one compose? He did!

parts.note: tar is a pitch-like substance
a tin is a can
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone with a sense of pitch can compose; this man could.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He did!' refers back to composing: he is a composer. 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Tartini was an Italian Baroque violinist who composed the Devil's Trill Sonata.

clue.text: Delouse, as it were, when climbing with spikes

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: a made-up verb meaning remove the nits

explanation.surface: Ridding someone of lice while climbing with spiked boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine is a prong, so something tined has prongs or spikes.

clue.text: Not one of us? Not even him abroad?

parts.note: an odd number is not even
a man is a him
abroad means out of doors, out

explanation.surface: Asking whether an outsider abroad is not even one of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not fit in with a group is the one left over, the misfit.

clue.text: Congressman's acknowledgement?

parts.note: read not as a US politician but as a man having sexual congress, whose word for it is also the radio operator's 'message received'

explanation.definitionFit: The word is radio slang for 'understood' and British slang for having sex, which is 'congress'.

clue.text: Romance in the air?

parts.note: not a feeling of love about to happen but a love song carried on the evening air

explanation.definitionFit: A romance is also a lyrical song, and this one is sung outdoors beneath a lover's window.

clue.text: Horse sick around the withers initially; get a cloth!

parts.note: the horse is mounted soldiers, cavalry

indicators.note: takes the first letters of the words the and withers

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A horse is unwell around its withers, so fetch a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' suggests one animal, but it means mounted troops. 'around' and 'get a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a strong woollen twill fabric originally used for riding breeches.

clue.text: Japanese arrangements getting thumbs down among flatpack floggers

indicators.note: one word placed among the letters of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish retailer that sells flatpack furniture
a thumbs down is a refusal or BAN

explanation.surface: Japanese floral displays getting the thumbs down from a flatpack furniture shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of arranging flowers, so its products are arrangements.

clue.text: Hoosiers at home with Artemis here?

parts.note: in means at home
Diana is the Roman counterpart of the Greek goddess Artemis

explanation.surface: Asking whether the people of an American state keep a Greek goddess at home with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces and 'here?' is a link pointing to the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoosiers is the nickname for people from this Midwestern US state, used here for the state itself.

clue.text: Bell knell isn't muffled

indicators.note: the name is wrapped up, muffled, within the words knell isn't

explanation.surface: A bell rings out a death knell that is not dampened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell' looks like part of the bell-ringing picture, but it is the surname in a pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë published under the pseudonym of the Bell family name with this first name.

clue.text: "Young _____ is come out of the West" (Scott). See! See! In China, right?

definitions.text: "Young _____ is come out of the West" (Scott)

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see!

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the country

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: An excited cry about something seen in China, seeking confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Scott's ballad in Marmion opens with this line about the young hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The line fills the blank with the name of the knight in Scott's poem Marmion.

clue.text: Novelist nicking lines from Molière, lazy hack!

indicators.note: stealing, so letters are taken away
says which words the lines are stolen out of
to hack is to chop roughly, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: RY, railway, is the crossword abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A novelist steals verses from Molière, the lazy hack.
explanation.walkthrough: Take RY out of MOLIERE LAZY and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Germinal and Nana was a celebrated French novelist of the naturalist school.

clue.text: Ripped off old Arafat's lot with change of diet

parts.note: ex means former, old
Yasser Arafat led the PLO, the Palestine Liberation Organization

indicators.note: the diet is changed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheated by the old Arafat movement that changed its diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exploited is to be taken advantage of, cheated or swindled.

clue.text: What could restore amour-propre? French state bringing in experts

indicators.note: the outer letters take the experts inside them

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
aces are experts

explanation.surface: Asking what a proud French nation, calling in specialists, might do to regain its self-respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour-propre is self-esteem, and something that saves one's face spares it from humiliation.

clue.text: Move so move accepted, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A proposal is moved, so the motion is accepted perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a committee motion; the first 'Move' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leaving quickly, clearing off.

clue.text: So Hal was appropriate, according to The Listener!

parts.note: to appropriate is to steal, rob
otic means relating to the ear, the listener's organ

explanation.surface: Something was fitting according to The Listener crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Hal is the computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey. 'The Listener' suggests the crossword series but means the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hal was a mechanical intelligence, so machine-like in nature.

clue.text: Safe accommodation detached from college

indicators.note: one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: Peterhouse is the oldest college at Cambridge University
a house is accommodation

explanation.surface: A safe place to live set apart from the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: in old criminal slang a strongbox is a peter.
explanation.definitionFit: In underworld slang a safe was called a peter, hence safebreakers were peter-men.

clue.text: Is society sustained by good memory of Virgil, spatially?

indicators.note: held up inside, so the first pieces go within the others

parts.note: ROM is read-only computer memory
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a society is kept going by good recollection of the Roman poet Virgil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgil' suggests the Roman poet, but 'spatially' points to the astronaut Virgil 'Gus' Grissom.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil Grissom was an American astronaut of the Mercury and Gemini space programmes.

clue.text: Fish on a fat-free diet

parts.note: a small fish that shares its name with Jack of the nursery rhyme, who could eat no fat

explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like fish, and the surname of the rhyme's Jack who could eat no fat.

clue.text: Flat feast? Don't hold your breath!

definitions.meaning: a burst tyre, which leaves it flat
an instruction to expel the air

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a tyre burst, a lavish meal, and literally to expel air from the lungs.

clue.text: Irish bard detailed indication of a musical option

indicators.note: de-tailed, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Ossian is the legendary Irish poet

explanation.surface: An Irish poet gives detailed directions for a musical alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: In a score this Italian word marks an alternative passage the performer may play instead.

clue.text: Perform one in public and tire oneself out

indicators.note: one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: overt means open, public
to do is to perform
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Doing a turn in public and exhausting yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself too much is to exhaust oneself, an idiomatic sense of tiring out.

clue.text: It's old-time retro for this song writer

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
OT is the abbreviation for Old Testament, the old-time scripture

explanation.surface: A songwriter whose style is old-fashioned and retro.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Tosti was an Italian composer of popular parlour songs such as Goodbye.

clue.text: He investigated for 13 20s shortly before cathedral collapsed

indicators.note: a collapsed building is a heap of rearranged pieces
cut short, so the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone investigating something just before a cathedral fell down.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 and 20 are ELLIS and PETER, so '13 20s' is Ellis Peters, author of the medieval monk-detective novels. BEFOR (shortened 'before') and CATHEDRAL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Benedictine monk detective of Shrewsbury Abbey was created by novelist Ellis Peters.
